questions.q: Which of the following is true about motivation?
options: It has a willingness to activate but not channel the attitudes of learners
questions.explanation: Motivation is an internal psychological process that both activates and directs (channels) behavior. It is not merely a physical impulse, not purely external, and it does channel behavior, so none of the statements is true.

questions.q: The term "motivation" comes from a ____ word.
questions.explanation: Motivation derives from the Latin word 'movere', meaning to move. It reflects the idea that motivation is what moves a person to act.

questions.q: It is called extrinsic motivation if causal factor is ____.
questions.explanation: Extrinsic motivation comes from outside the person, such as rewards, punishments, or social pressure. Curiosity and self-satisfaction are internal sources, i.e. intrinsic motivation.

questions.q: ____ motivation is considered to be more crucial for students as it is associated with deep learning, better performance and self-efficacy.
questions.explanation: Intrinsic motivation, doing something for its own interest and enjoyment, is linked to deeper processing, persistence, and stronger self-efficacy. Extrinsic and introjected (guilt- or ego-driven) motivation tend to produce more surface-level learning.

questions.q: ____ proposed that there are three primary drives that drive human behavior.
questions.explanation: Clark Hull's drive-reduction theory holds that behavior is driven by primary biological drives (such as hunger, thirst, and sex) that create tension the organism seeks to reduce. Watson, Piaget, and the Gestalt school did not propose a drive theory of motivation.

questions.q: Expectancy Theory of Motivation was developed by ____.
questions.explanation: Victor Vroom proposed expectancy theory in 1964, stating that motivation depends on expectancy, instrumentality, and valence. Hull is associated with drive theory and Murray with the theory of psychogenic needs.

questions.q: An example of ____ is thinking, "If I work hard I can achieve the targets my boss has set for me".
questions.explanation: Expectancy is the belief that effort will lead to successful performance. Instrumentality would be the belief that performance leads to a reward, and valence is how much the reward is valued.

questions.q: In SMART goals, T stands for ____.
questions.explanation: SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-based (or time-bound). A deadline gives the goal urgency and a point at which to evaluate progress.

questions.q: Friendship is a ____ need in Maslow's hierarchy.
questions.explanation: Maslow's third level, love and belonging, covers friendship, intimacy, family, and social connection. Esteem needs concern respect and recognition, not affiliation.

questions.q: ____ theory differentiates between autonomous motivation and controlled motivation.
questions.explanation: Deci and Ryan's self-determination theory distinguishes autonomous motivation (acting from genuine choice and interest) from controlled motivation (acting from external pressure or internal guilt). The other theories do not make this distinction.
